This cracking sound only happens when I pedal. Is it possible that its a bearing? is there a simple-ish fix?
I have a cracking sound in my crank
After miles of hard riding and washing dirt off, some of the grease can breakdown or wash out. I usually regrease after every 150 miles.

Bottom Brackets and Cranks... I f you develop a creak or cracking noise it is either going to be your pedals, the crank to bottom bracket interface, or the bottom bracket to frame interface. Usually it is the bottom bracket to frame interface, some small piece of grit has made it between the BB and frame and is now causing awful noises. After that, it is usually the bearings followed by pedals.

Before I started using a crank with a 30mm spindle, I was using Sram X0 and XTR before that. While the Sram bottom bracket was never that great, not compared to a Chris King with ease of serviceability, they both were loads better than the current RaceFace bottom brackets I have been using. The RaceFace bottom brackets seem to have extremely tight seals on the bearings which causes a lot of friction but, in the end, does not keep grit out. I am on my third RaceFace bottom bracket with each being pulled at around the 250 mile mark. This is riding races with wet muddy conditions so it is putting them to the test but they just don't compare to what I am used to.

So, rant over and back to your problem:
You are going to want to pull the crank and should just go ahead and pull the bottom bracket off your frame. Clean the mud off everything and use a wire brush to clean the threads on the bottom bracket and the frame. Get them as clean as you can as one sand grain can cause loud creaking noises.

At this point, if you are up to it and depending on the type of bottom bracket you have, you can pull the dust seals off the bearings and clean out the bearings with degreaser, then WD-40, then a light lube, and finally re-pack them with grease.

It is not worth it if you are wondering whether you should pull the bearing apart and look at the ball bearings - most cartridge bearings aren't worth that much effort.

The go-to grease for this is Phil Wood's grease, not their Tenacious Oil/grease but their regular bearing grease. I have also used Finish Line's Ceramic Grease and various greases from Tri-Flow - all with good results. Reassemble the bearings by placing the dust seals back on.

Now, go to your frame. You can use grease on the threads in your frame or you can even use anti-seize compound. You can be reasonably liberal in how much grease you put down in the threads but, remember, grease can also trap dirt.

Clean your cranks. Take your pedals off and clean the threads. Grease the threads or use anti-seize on them as well. If you are feeling up to it and your pedals are easy to work on, clean the bearings on them and re-grease them as well.

Reassemble using the proper torque settings. You should be good to go.

Do your research, but don't stress it. If you get hung up on a concept, have a vet explain it to you. And play, play play. Simple at first, but add some complexity here and there.

You're right about having one person power through the reading — that person should be the Dungeon Master. The DM shouldn't participate as a player character, and the players shouldn't be reading through the adventure. Since you're the one asking the question, you should probably be the Dungeon Master.
